entry_point.code: SymCryptXmssRandomizedHash(&pKey->params, Idx, Randomness, pKey->Root, pbMessage, cbMessage, RandomizedHash);

trace.code: SymCryptXmssSetParams validates cbHashOutput only as: == 0 || > pHash->resultSize || > SYMCRYPT_HASH_MAX_RESULT_SIZE — so n = 1..7 is ACCEPTED (SHA-256 resultSize=32, n=4 passes)
SYMCRYPT_STORE_MSBFIRST64(&idxBuf[cbHashOutput - sizeof(Idx)], Idx) — with n=4 the index is -4: the 8-byte big-endian Idx store lands 4 bytes BELOW idxBuf

critic-verified: the below-buffer 4 bytes are the spilled pbMsg pointer slot — the Idx store zeroes its high 4 bytes (the sign index's upper bytes are 0), truncating the 64-bit pointer to 32 bits; the subsequent SymCryptHashAppend on the truncated pointer crashes (SIGSEGV observed)

preconditions: A caller creates a custom XMSS parameter set with cbHashOutput (n) in 1..7 via the public SymCryptXmssSetParams API and signs a message

Custom parameter sets are an explicitly supported feature; no attacker data is required for the memory corruption itself (local API misuse triggers it; a remote attacker needs an app exposing custom XMSS config — none known)

evidence.fixed_commit: 2b930b400e39f541a0b0245796382d79d8c4db72 (class fix, cbPrefix bounds for custom XMSS parameter sets — the cbHashOutput gap was left unfixed)
evidence.vulnerable_version: HEAD 286762b (v103.13.0); the unchecked index dates to the XMSS implementation (15d0779)
evidence.observed_result: REAL-CODE differential (SymCrypt compiled from source with zig cc): VULNERABLE build -> SymCryptXmssSetParams(n=4,h=10,w=4) returns SYMCRYPT_NO_ERROR, keygen succeeds, SymCryptXmssSign SIGSEGVs (rc=139) — the Idx store zeroes the high half of the spilled pbMsg pointer (critic disassembly-verified) and the truncated-pointer hash append crashes. FIXED build (cbHashOutput < sizeof(UINT64) rejected) -> SymCryptXmssSetParams returns SYMCRYPT_INVALID_ARGUMENT (0x800e), no crash. Same caller code; only the parameter validation differs. DoS-class (C:N/I:N), hence medium severity per the critic pass.
